children: shares fell more than 2% Friday after Morgan Stanley lowered its rating on the drugmaker, citing longer-term risks tied to semaglutide and pressure from potential generic competition.

The brokerage moved the stock to Underweight from Equal-weight. It expects semaglutide to account for about 75% of Novo's sales in 2026, leaving the company exposed to the loss of exclusivity beginning in 2031.

Morgan Stanley expects Novo's oral obesity business to generate $10 billion by 2031. However, analyst Thibault Boutherin said that business may not fully offset the impact from semaglutide-related pricing pressure.

The firm also flagged weaker momentum in U.S. prescriptions for the Wegovy pill following a stronger first half of 2026. Eli Lilly (LLY), meanwhile, has been taking a large share of Medicare demand through its Zepbound product under the Bridge program.

Novo and Lilly remain major players in obesity treatments, with both developing oral and injectable therapies. Novo recently reported positive results from a pediatric semaglutide study, with 40.4% of treated children no longer classified as having obesity after 68 weeks.

title: Novo Nordisk Stock Plunges on Morgan Stanley Downgrade Warns of Semaglutide Patent Cliff
